distractors.value: You can't shade more than one whole circle

diagnostic_item.stem: These pictures show 1 whole circle fully shaded and one more circle with 1/4 shaded. What fraction is shaded overall?

intervention.script: Let's shade one WHOLE circle, then start shading a second one — that extra piece is what makes it more than one whole.

learner_evidence.explanation: it's 5/4 because the first circle is a whole one which is 4/4 and then one more piece makes 5/4

caveats: transfer confirmed on a number line only; set-model transfer not yet attempted
mastery_outcome.claim: Ava can represent fractions greater than one whole

misconception.citation: Literature on the part-whole-only conception of fractions and the transition to fractions greater than one.
misconception.cognitive_origin: Early fraction experience is almost entirely parts of a single whole (pizza slices, pie charts), so 'fraction' gets encoded as inherently less than one; a numerator larger than the denominator is treated as an error rather than a quantity greater than one whole.
sprout_forbidden: stating a fraction can be greater than one whole before resolution
misconception.title: A fraction can never be greater than one whole

skill.title: Represent fractions greater than one whole

sprout_forbidden: stating a fraction can be greater than one whole before resolution

sprout_scripts.utterance: That fraction can't be right — the top number can't be bigger than the bottom!
Wait, can a fraction ever be bigger than one whole thing?
I thought fractions were always pieces smaller than one whole.
